title: Mission-aligned Onboarding and Role Succession Toolkit
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

This toolkit defines a mission-aligned approach to onboarding, role succession, and internal tool access at Redwood. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, ICs transitioning to manager roles, and platform owners responsible for provisioning tools. The playbook emphasizes repeatable 30/60/90 day onboarding sprints, explicit role success criteria, and a lightweight succession path for critical roles.

Scope:

- Applies to all full-time and long-term contractors joining engineering, product, and platform teams.
- Includes: onboarding cadence, role competency checkpoints, manager handoff checklist, and the tool access matrix and request process.
- Excludes: temporary event-based access (see Security-and-compliance playbooks).

Objectives:

1. Reduce time-to-impact for new hires to 8 weeks for measurable contribution (first merged PR, shipped doc, or owned customer call).
2. Provide a clear, inspectable path for role succession for 20 critical roles (service owners, infra leads, SRE on-call rotation leads).
3. Standardize tool access requests to reduce approval time to <24 hours for low-risk tooling and <72 hours for elevated privileges.

Who should use this doc:

- Hiring managers (create 30/60/90 goals)
- People Ops (coordinate access, run onboarding cohorts)
- Team leads (validate capability checkpoints)
- Platform owners (maintain tool catalog)

Key definitions:

- Mission-aligned onboarding sprint: a focused 30-day plan with specific deliverables tied to product metrics or team goals.
- Role succession candidate: an internal IC/PM/EM with documented readiness and a 1:1 development plan.
- Low-risk tool: read-only dashboards, Slack channels, non-production GCP viewer roles.
- Elevated tool: production IAM, KMS access, SRE runbook edit privileges.

1) 30/60/90 Onboarding Sprint (template)

- Day 0 (Preboarding)
  1. Account provisioning initiated: Okta invite sent, GitHub team membership requested, Slack join links provided.
  2. Hardware and workspace: Mac/PC ordered or desk stipend scheduled.
  3. Pre-read packet shared: team charter, product brief, architecture diagram links.

- Week 1–2 (30 day goals)
  - Orientation sessions: security, benefits, payroll, and dev-environment setup.
  - Deliverable: clone repo(s) and open first non-trivial PR; pair with buddy.
  - Checkpoint: manager sign-off ("environment ready / can run tests locally").

- Week 3–6 (60 day goals)
  - Deliverable: own a minor feature or bug fix end-to-end (design -> test -> deploy).
  - Completion: demo at team sync; update runbook or docs describing the feature.
  - Checkpoint: competency review against rubric (see Role Competency Matrix).

- Week 7–12 (90 day goals)
  - Deliverable: deliver measurable impact (e.g., reduce latency by X ms, improve dashboard coverage).
  - Outcome: candidate added to rotation or given medium-sized project ownership.
  - Checkpoint: 90-day review with People Ops and hiring manager; document next-step learning plan.

2) Role Competency Matrix (summary)

| Role level | Ownership expectations | Observable signals | Example activities |
|---|---:|---|---|
| IC-1 / New IC | Ship small PRs, follow playbooks | PR cycles, passing tests | Fix bug, write doc |
| IC-2 / Experienced IC | Ship features, mentor juniors | Peer reviews, design notes | Lead small cross-team task |
| IC-3 / Senior IC | Architectural influence, service ownership | Incident leadership, design ownership | Lead design review, own SLA |
| EM-1 / Manager | People development, delivery | 1:1s cadence, roadmap delivery | Run retrospective, hire checklist |

Note: Full rubric lives on /confluence/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/competency-maps-and-rotation-paths-2027 (linked under Related Pages).

3) Succession Playbook for Critical Roles

Purpose: Ensure continuity for service owners and platform leads when planned or unplanned transitions occur.

Process (for each identified critical role):
1. Maintain a "Role Card" (one-pager) owned by the current role holder: responsibilities, runbooks, escalation path, key contacts, and current health indicators.
2. Identify at least two potential successors (primary, secondary) with readiness notes and a 3-6 month ramp plan.
3. Quarterly readiness check: manager + People Ops to review progress and adjust the development plan.
4. Handover: 2-week overlap shadowing for operational roles; for strategic roles, 4–8 week transition period recommended.

Ownership:
- People Ops: track Role Cards for all critical roles and maintain the Succession Dashboard.
- Team Manager: nominate successors and approve ramp plans.
- Current Role Holder: keep runbooks and Role Card current.

4) Internal Tools Access Matrix (abridged)

| Tool / Service | Typical audience | Access type | Request channel | Approval owner | SLA target |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Slack private channels | Team members | Member | self-join via onboarding checklist | Team lead | 4 hours |
| GitHub team | Engineering | Write (repo-specific) | GitHub access request form | Repo owner | 24 hours |
| CI/CD (Buildkite) | Engineers | Trigger / edit | Okta ticket / internal form | SRE lead | 24 hours |
| Staging GCP project | Devs, QA | Editor (non-prod) | Internal infra ticket | Infra eng owner | 48 hours |
| Production GCP IAM | SREs, Infra | Elevated (prod roles) | Elevated access request (Jira) | Security + Infra approval | 72 hours |
| KMS / HSM | Platform SRE | Key admin | Security request (Jira) | Security | 5 business days |

Requesting access (step-by-step)

1. Determine risk level: review row in matrix.
2. Use 'Access Request' template (Confluence link in Related Pages) and attach justification.
3. Submit via Jira project REDWOOD-SEC-ACCESS with label 'access-request' and include manager approval comment.
4. Security triages within SLA target and attaches checklist for elevated requests.

CLI snippets (examples):

- GitHub team request (example comment template):
  ```
  /request-access github-team:team-name reason:"Onboarded as backend engineer for payments, needs repo write for x-service" approver:@manager
  ```

- Infrastructure read-only GCP access (self-service):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.ai/access-requests \\n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" \\n    -d '{"resource":"projects/staging","role":"viewer","reason":"onboarding - test env"}'
  ```

5) Manager Handoff Checklist (when a hire leaves or role rotates)

- Document updates: ensure Role Card, runbooks, and oncall playbooks are current.
- Knowledge transfer: schedule 2–4 shadow sessions, record critical demos, and add notes to Confluence.
- Access changes: rotate any shared secrets, reassign service accounts if necessary.
- Communications: notify upstream/downstream teams and update owner fields in service catalog.

6) Development Sprints for Succession (quarterly cadence)

- Each quarter, teams nominate 1–2 internal candidates for development sprints focused on mission-aligned outcomes (e.g., reduce 95th percentile latency, implement better test coverage).
- Sprints are 6 weeks with a deliverable and a post-mortem presented at the engineering all-hands.

7) Benefits & Hybrid Work Notes (ops-focused)

- Workplace stipends are approved during onboarding and tracked in the Onboarding Toolchain (Finance link).
- Flexible return policy: teams set a 3-day in-office baseline unless customer needs require otherwise; exceptions require manager + People Ops approval.

8) Escalations and Exceptions

- If access is required urgently for production incident triage, use the "incident access" flow: Pager duty -> Incident Commander documents need -> Security emergency approval channel.
- Exceptions to the SLA targets must be logged on the request and reviewed weekly by People Ops + Security.

9) Templates and Attachments (quick links)

- 30/60/90 template (copy-on-use)
- Role Card template (one-pager)
- Access Request template (for JIRA)
- Manager handoff checklist (GDoc)
- Succession Dashboard (Looker slice)

10) Change log and governance

- Document owner: People Ops (Maya Chen). Major changes require reviewer sign-off list.
- Review cadence: annual review plus ad-hoc updates after incidents or major org changes.

FAQ (short)

Q: Who approves access to production IAM?
A: Security + Infra owners; approval documented in Jira ticket.

Q: How do I nominate a successor?
A: Add nominee to the Role Card and schedule a readiness review with People Ops.

Q: Where are Role Cards stored?
A: Role Cards live in the Succession Dashboard and are linked from each team's Confluence space.

Contact and escalation

- Primary owner: Maya Chen (People Ops) — people-ops@redwood.ai
- Security escalation: security-ops@redwood.ai
- Platform provisioning: infra-oncall@redwood.ai

This playbook is intended as an operational manual to reduce onboarding friction, make succession predictable, and centralize tool access decisions. Please propose edits via the Confluence edit workflow or file a People Ops ticket for substantial changes.
